title: Service viability gates and autoscale harmonization
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: During multi-region failovers and sudden request surges some services either overreact (autoscaler thrash) or underreact (latency SLOs violated). Existing probe-driven readiness logic treats all failures uniformly which leads to large-scale failover storms, late warmups for new replicas, and inconsistent circuit-breaker behavior for token-heavy versus request-heavy workloads.

Goal: Implement a lightweight "viability gate" layer that sits before canonical readiness transitions and works with the autoscaler to harmonize scale-up/scale-down decisions and circuit-breaker degradation choices. The gate computes a composite viability score from synthetic canaries, probe latency percentiles, KV cache hit ratio, and recent per-token load. Autoscaler decisions will respect a lease/warmup handshake and a throttled ramp policy to prevent thrash. Circuit breakers will use weighted degradation (token-weighted + request-priority) rather than binary open/closed.

High-level approach:
- Design a viability gate component (k8s admission-like controller) that emits a per-replica composite viability score and a readiness hint (GREEN/YELLOW/RED).
- Modify readiness transition logic to consult viability hint: RED prevents Ready; YELLOW permits Ready but marks replica as low-priority for routing and autoscaler weighting.
- Autoscaler harmonization: introduce a scale lease and warmup handshake. New replicas must signal warmup-complete via viability score before being counted for fast path routing. Scale-down uses a graceful drain window proportional to recent token-weighted traffic.
- Circuit breaker behavior: implement priority-aware shedding: shed tail-latency-heavy or low-priority routes first; token-heavy requests get softer shedding thresholds but earlier routing to Dedicated variants or variants with higher token budgets.
- Simulation & safe rollout: run a chaos + spike simulation harness to validate no single-region probe failure causes global thrash. Blue-green rollout with feature flag and stepwise regional enabling.
acceptance_criteria: Viability gate publishes per-replica score (0-100) and readiness hint to telemetry (pm-viability-score metric) and is sampled in the console dashboard
Autoscaler respects warmup handshake: new replicas not counted for aggressive scale targets until viability score >= 70 for 30s
Circuit breakers perform request-priority shedding: P0 and authenticated traffic prioritized; non-critical batch routes shed first
Integration tests (simulation harness) show <3% request loss and SLO compliance (p95 latency within target) under a synthetic regional failover with 3x baseline load
No regression in median latency for steady-state traffic (±5%) and no autoscaler thrash in 30-minute soak in preprod
tasks: Design viability score schema and thresholds (RFC)
Implement viability gate controller and lightweight API for readiness hints
Instrument runtime to emit components used by score: canary latency, probe p99/p95, KV cache hit ratio, token-weighted recent load
Add autoscaler lease/warmup handshake and modify replica counting logic
Implement weighted circuit-breaker logic in routing layer
Build simulation harness scenarios and run end-to-end tests
Create dashboards and alerts for pm-viability-score, autoscale lease breaches, and shedding events
Plan gradual rollout with feature flag and regional gating

2026-02-25 Jonas Reed: RFC draft posted (link below). Prototype viability gate implemented in sim harness; initial scoring function uses weighted sum with tunable weights. Observed that KV cache hit ratio has higher signal for degration in our workloads than raw probe failures.

2026-03-02 Priya Desai (SRE): Feedback from SRE review: ensure score is explainable and include 'reason' tags for RED/YELLOW states to aid on-call. Request additional telemetry for token-weighted evictions and per-route shedding counts.

2026-03-07 Jonas Reed: Completed autoscaler lease implementation in branch eng/viability/autoscale-lease. Added warmup timeout and scaledown-grace proportional to token-weighted request rate. Running preprod soak now.

2026-03-10 Aisha Malik: Simulation results attached showed a reduction in autoscaler churn from 42 events/hour to 6 events/hour under simulated probe flapping. Preparing rollout plan for two canary regions next week.
